overview: This Senate resolution designates September 2026 as "National Spinal Cord Injury Awareness Month." It notes that about 311,560 Americans live with spinal cord injuries, with roughly 18,482 new injuries a year, that more than 42,000 of those living with them are veterans, and that car crashes are the leading cause. It says life expectancy for people with these injuries has not improved much since the 1980s and calls for new treatments to prevent and reverse paralysis. The resolution supports research and clinical trials of promising therapies and commends the people and organizations working to improve the lives of those affected. The Senate approved it by unanimous consent on September 29, 2026.
for: Supporters say greater awareness can encourage safer driving and build support for research toward better treatments and a cure for paralysis.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic: it does not change any law or provide new funding for spinal cord injury research.
